freeCopyCases: First copy for each date of service needed for a qualified claim or appeal (Social Security Act or a federal or state needs-based benefit program), once per calendar year (78B-5-618(12)(a))
All fees waived for an indigent individual (household income at or below 100% of the federal poverty level), one free copy per date of service per provider per year (78B-5-618(13))
feeRules: Patient or personal representative: "may charge a reasonable cost-based fee provided that the fee includes only the cost of:" copying and postage (78B-5-618(4)(b))

Attorney or other third party: $30 per request to locate records; 53 cents per page for first 40 pages, 32 cents after; $20 certification; $20 expedite fee; inflation-adjusted yearly (78B-5-618(5), (11))
Electronic copy: per page fee is 50% of the paper fee; cap of $150; cap falls to $75 if late past 30 days and free if late past 60 days (78B-5-618(10))
Second or later copy for a qualified claim or appeal: up to 60 cents per page, no administrative fee (78B-5-618(12)(b))

provisions.title: Patient access to medical records: fee waiver for indigent individuals
provisions.quote: shall waive all fees under this section for an indigent individual.
provisions.appliesTo: Health care providers and their third-party record services; indigent means household income at or below 100% of the federal poverty level.

provisions.title: Patient access to medical records: deadline for patient copies
provisions.quote: shall provide the copy within the deadlines required by the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996, Administrative Simplification rule, 45 C.F.R. Sec. 164.524(b);

copy_rights.note: Free copy element met: a first copy for a benefits claim or appeal is free, and copies are free for indigent people. Both go beyond HIPAA and 45 CFR 171.302. The deadline follows HIPAA, so no shorter deadline.

crossCheck.note: beyondFederalFloor yes: a free first copy for a benefits claim or appeal goes past 164.524 and 171.302. Deadlines stay at 30 days. The indigent waiver opens with an exception for Subsections (4) through (8).
